pillar_reactions.evidence: Flat acceptance — 'No, that makes sense. Right.' The reaction is muted because he had already absorbed the content elsewhere; the rep noticed and said so: 'I have this, like, weird feeling that you already somewhat know how the program is designed,' answered 'I've definitely seen a lot of his content.' The one moment of real engagement came earlier when the rep contrasted his current five-part gym session with three to four 30-40 minute kettlebell sessions, drawing 'Okay, I wouldn't be able to do that. No way.' He also interrupted the pillar to ask price — 'How much is it by the way? Like what's the pricing model?' — which the rep deferred.

Accepted the what/when/how-much frame with 'No, feel straightforward. Right,' then asked the one mechanics question that mattered to him: 'And so he prepares a meal plan to follow?' The rep had tailored this pillar well, feeding back the prospect's own admission that he under-eats — 'you mentioned that you feel that you're not eating enough, and that's quite common... that's going to be one thing that Trevor needs to dial in, which is protein intake' — and flagging the pre-bed Greek yogurt as a sleep and recovery problem. No pushback on the eight-hour window; he had already told the rep that fasted morning training made sense to him.

'No, that all makes sense to me.' The rep correctly identified this as the decisive pillar for him — 'I think this is the crucial one for you because you mentioned that you somewhat haven't been consistent with that' — and tied the weekly check-in to his stated muscle-gain goal and the cell-phone access to his travel weeks. Despite the accurate targeting the reaction stayed neutral; unlike the Steve Dawson call, accountability did not draw an enthusiastic response even though the prospect's own diagnosis was inconsistency.

SECOND, UNRESOLVED REACTION on the delivery mechanic rather than the content. He raised it before the pillars and it was never answered: 'I am a little skeptical at like how the video filming and the communication and all that stuff's going to work, but I I'm, I'm ready to kind of see how that plays out.' Given that he also said 'it takes much longer than the average person for me to understand a movement' and 'I do need to be told if I'm doing something wrong', the asynchronous video-feedback loop is the single mechanic this buyer most needed demonstrated, and it never was.

anchors.raw: I pay my personal trainer far more than that. So that's fine. Or I mean, that's not far more, actually pretty similar, but I mean, I understand, right? It takes someone's time and effort and it's also a skill. So to me, I'm not afraid of paying someone for what they're worth.
anchors.competitor: Atlanta-based personal trainer (three sessions/week over four years)
anchors.note: The strongest supportive anchor anywhere in this batch — the buyer benchmarked $6,000 against his existing spend unprompted and concluded it was comparable, then volunteered a value justification on the rep's behalf. He had already converted the number himself ('a thousand per month, about'). The trainer relationship is also ending as he relocates, so the budget is being freed at exactly the right moment. The rep did not have to defend the price at any point.

anchors.raw: I also see that Trevor has, you know, over a million followers. I like that he's remarkably consistent with what he says. He's not really saying anything new when he makes a video, which I like that because that means he means what he says, right? He's not being gimmicky.
anchors.note: Pre-sold by content over a year or more on TikTok and Instagram before ever booking. He supplied the credibility argument himself and then supplied the rebuttal to his own scam objection. Worth noting for attribution: this deal was made by the content, not by the call.

anchors.raw: I've never done an online coach before and I'm not going to like kind of like generally think it's like a scam because there's so many online scammers
anchors.note: Category-level rather than product-level distrust, and it resolved on the call. Recorded because it is the second consecutive prospect in this batch to raise unprompted doubts about the legitimacy of paid online coaching, which suggests the category headwind is systematic rather than incidental.

anchors.raw: in last year, I went on a pretty insane diet, and I lost 30 pounds in one month, no peptides, no nothing, just straight up clean eating
anchors.note: A prior self-managed result at zero cost. He believes he can execute alone when locked in — 'I was dropping weight, gaining muscle' — and his own diagnosis is that the discipline is not durable ('there will always come a point where I'm like...'). Untouched by the rep, this anchor supports a do-it-myself-again alternative rather than the programme.

unmet_demand.want: Coaching on breathing — he is a shallow chest breather, not a nose breather under load, and holds his breath through every lift despite his trainer correcting him. Also named pelvic floor work specifically.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Raised as one of his headline items and never addressed at any point in the call, including throughout the training and mobility pillar. Kettlebell work almost certainly does train breathing mechanics under load, so this is very likely served and simply never claimed. A named, unanswered goal is a real risk of post-purchase disappointment.

unmet_demand.want: A demonstration of how the video-feedback and communication loop actually works before committing
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He said outright he was skeptical of it, and it is the mechanic his stated learning difficulty depends on most. The rep described it twice in the abstract but never showed the app, a submission or a sample feedback video — all of which he had available, having screen-shared the app on another call that same week.

unmet_demand.want: To pay online, in his own time, without scheduling a second call
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Refused as procedure — 'I need to be on a call with you... we have a procedure that I get you onboarded, get you in the community.' This is a sales-process constraint rather than a product limitation, and it is what prevented the sale completing on the day.

unmet_demand.want: Food allergy and inflammation testing with bloodwork to identify what is driving his tightness and suspected gluten reaction
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Outside the offer entirely. He is arranging it independently — 'I also plan on doing a food and allergy test just to figure out what is causing my inflammation and getting some blood work done related to that' — and the rep did not engage with it. This is the second prospect in the batch buying clinical-adjacent testing the programme does not provide.
